\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جیب} \ur{کترا} (jeb katrā)}{جیب کترا (jeb katrā)}]{\ur{جیب} \ur{کترا} (jeb katrā) — a pickpocket}

\label{lesson:UR-C277-jeb-katra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a witness, then the Urdu for a crime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جیب} \ur{کترا}}
\textbf{\ur{جیب} \ur{کترا}} — \emph{jeb katrā} — \textquotedblleft{}a pickpocket\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بس} \ur{میں} \ur{ایک} \ur{جیب} \ur{کترا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bas meṅ ek jeb katrā thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a pickpocket on the bus.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جیب} \ur{کترا}} (\emph{jeb katrā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{جیب}}, a pocket, usually traced to Persian \emph{jēb}, and \emph{katrā}, one who snips, from \emph{katarnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to clip\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{kartarī}, \textquotedblleft{}scissors\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2858): the one who cuts into pockets.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jeb katrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jeb katrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bas meṅ ek jeb katrā thā.} — There was a pickpocket on the bus.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a witness, then the Urdu for a crime, then say \emph{jeb katrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جیب} \ur{کترا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pickpocket\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چھیننا} (chhīnnā)}{چھیننا (chhīnnā)}]{\ur{چھیننا} (chhīnnā) — to snatch}

\label{lesson:UR-C277-chhinna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crime, then the Urdu for a pickpocket.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چھیننا}}
\textbf{\ur{چھیننا}} — \emph{chhīnnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to snatch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{میرا} \ur{موبائل} \ur{چھینا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne merā mobāil chhīnā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He snatched my mobile.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{تھیلا} \ur{چھینا}, \emph{us ne thailā chhīnā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چھیننا}} (\emph{chhīnnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{chīnnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to snatch, to pluck\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{chinná}, \textquotedblleft{}cut off\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5047). It is taking by force, in one quick pull.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhīnnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhīnnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne merā mobāil chhīnā.} — He snatched my mobile.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a crime, then the Urdu for a pickpocket, then say \emph{chhīnnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{چھیننا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To snatch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جھپٹنا} (jhapaṭnā)}{جھپٹنا (jhapaṭnā)}]{\ur{جھپٹنا} (jhapaṭnā) — to swoop; to pounce}

\label{lesson:UR-C277-jhapatna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a pickpocket, then the Urdu for to snatch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جھپٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جھپٹنا}} — \emph{jhapaṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to swoop; to pounce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چور} \ur{تھیلے} \ur{پر} \ur{جھپٹا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chor thaile par jhapaṭā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief swooped on the bag.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{تھیلے} \ur{پر} \ur{جھپٹا}, \emph{voh thaile par jhapaṭā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جھپٹنا}} (\emph{jhapaṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jhapaṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to run quickly\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*jhapp}, a jerk, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5336); in Urdu it is the sudden rush of a hawk or a thief: \textbf{\ur{تھیلے} \ur{پر} \ur{جھپٹا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhapaṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor thaile par jhapaṭā.} — The thief swooped on the bag.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a pickpocket, then the Urdu for to snatch, then say \emph{jhapaṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{فرار} (farār)}{فرار (farār)}]{\ur{فرار} (farār) — on the run; escaped}

\label{lesson:UR-C277-farar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to snatch, then the Urdu for to swoop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{فرار}}
\textbf{\ur{فرار}} — \emph{farār} — \textquotedblleft{}on the run; escaped\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چور} \ur{ابھی} \ur{تک} \ur{فرار} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chor abhī tak farār hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief is still on the run.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{فرار}} (\emph{farār}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{firār}, \textquotedblleft{}flight, running away\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\ur{فرار} \ur{ہے}} is still at large; \textbf{\ur{فرار} \ur{ہو} \ur{گیا}} has got away.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{farār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor abhī tak farār hai.} — The thief is still on the run.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to snatch, then the Urdu for to swoop, then say \emph{farār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مجرم} (mujrim)}{مجرم (mujrim)}]{\ur{مجرم} (mujrim) — a criminal}

\label{lesson:UR-C277-mujrim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to swoop, then the Urdu for on the run.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مجرم}}
\textbf{\ur{مجرم}} — \emph{mujrim} — \textquotedblleft{}a criminal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{پولیس} \ur{ہوتی} \ur{تو} \ur{مجرم} \ur{نہ} \ur{بھاگتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar polīs hotī to mujrim na bhāgtā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the police had been there, the criminal would not have run off.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مجرم}} (\emph{mujrim}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mujrim}, \textquotedblleft{}one who has done wrong\textquotedblright{}. It is the word of the courts and the papers for anyone who broke the law.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujrim}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujrim}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar polīs hotī to mujrim na bhāgtā.} — If the police had been there, the criminal would not have run off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to swoop, then the Urdu for on the run, then say \emph{mujrim} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مجرم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A criminal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
